hook.text: A modern tractor guided by GPS can plant seeds within 2 centimeters of the target—10,000 times across a field.

buildup.text: Precision agriculture uses sensors, drones, and GPS to apply exactly the right input in the right spot.

discovery.text: Variable-rate technology adjusts fertilizer and seed rates across a field based on real-time soil data.

twist.text: The technology is expensive. Small-scale farmers in developing countries—who need it most—can't afford it yet.

climax.text: Smartphone-based tools are bringing some precision techniques to smallholders—but the gap remains wide.

punchline.text: Farm by the centimeter, not the field. Precision saves inputs and soil.

quiz.question: What does variable-rate technology do?
options: Adjusts fertilizer and seed rates across a field based on soil data

details.summary: Precision agriculture uses GPS, sensors, drones, and data analytics to manage fields at a micro level. This topic covers variable-rate technology, yield mapping, and how data-driven farming applies the right input at the right place and time.
details.whyItMatters: Uniform field management wastes resources where they are not needed and under-treats areas that need more. Precision agriculture optimizes every square meter, increasing profit while reducing environmental impact.
takeaways: Yield maps reveal productivity variation of 50% or more within a single field
Precision agriculture can reduce fertilizer use by 15–20% without yield loss
The global precision agriculture market exceeds $7 billion and is growing fast

faq.question: What technologies make up precision agriculture?
faq.answer: Core technologies include GPS-guided tractors, soil and crop sensors, drone and satellite imagery, variable-rate applicators, yield monitors, and farm management software that integrates data from all sources into actionable field-level decisions.

faq.question: How does precision agriculture benefit the environment?
faq.answer: By matching inputs precisely to field needs, precision agriculture reduces excess fertilizer that causes water pollution, cuts pesticide use through targeted application, lowers fuel consumption, and minimizes soil compaction from unnecessary passes.
